judgments.reasoning_cat1: The preamble leaves the execution date blank ('made as of June __, 2004'), an incompleteness that could matter to when obligations attached. Otherwise the parties and their roles are plainly identified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches Schedule A and the Section 1.1 'Member' definition (LSB and DMSA), so no relational conflict appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The recital garbles the statute's name ('pursuant to the Maine Lunited Liability Company'), leaving the defined 'Maine Act' introduced through a mangled phrase. That is a mechanical defect on the face of the recital.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article I separately defines 'Maine Act' correctly and Sections 2.1/2.3 track it, so the recital is repaired rather than contradicted by the operative text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard consideration language with nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It creates no operative obligation that could clash with Articles II-XVII.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 'unless the context otherwise requires' opener injects some flexibility but is boilerplate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It governs Article I definitions generally and conflicts with nothing specific.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure cross-reference definition with no ambiguity of its own.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 13.1 does define 'Additional Members', so the cross-reference holds.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Control' is defined by the familiar but inherently elastic 'power to direct or cause the direction of the management and policies', and the text contains an OCR-level punctuation slip. The vagueness is conventional rather than acute.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Affiliate' is used in Sections 3.1, 6.8(x) and 12.7 consistently with this meaning.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Self-referential and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 17.10's amendment mechanism.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear definition of 'Articles' with no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 10.1 refers to 'the Certificate', an undefined label that seems to mean the Articles, a minor mismatch traceable to that section rather than this one.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One-line definition, nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article VI creates the Board consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Simple cross-reference definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.4 does establish and maintain Capital Accounts as promised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Fair market value of any property' is a valuation standard but a familiar one.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Schedule A/Section 4.1 speak of 'agreed value' of contributions, a slightly different measure than fair market value.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard statutory-reference definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently in Articles VIII and XI.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite identification of the entity despite a typo in 'limited'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent throughout, though the 'Person' definition oddly reuses the word 'Company' for corporations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is a sprawling list ('any officers, directors, Members, partners, employees, representatives or agents of a Member... or their respective Affiliates') whose outer boundary is genuinely hard to fix. Its breadth invites argument about who is covered.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 17.11 confers rights only on Members and Managers, yet Sections 12.4-12.5 give indemnity rights to all Covered Persons, a real tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Circular but harmless one-line definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article VI supplies the substance.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three-limbed but mechanical definition of Fiscal Year.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Article VIII allocation provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The wording is garbled ('such Member's interest of the profits and losses') and mixes voting, profit and distribution rights into one term. It is unclear whether an 'Interest' is a unitary bundle or a countable unit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article XVI treats Interests as countable ('the aggregate Interests offered to be purchased exceeds the number to be transferred', 'number of LLC Votes'), which does not sit easily with this unitary definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb (iii) sweeps in 'all policies, practices and guidelines of any governmental body', a catch-all far broader than the enumerated binding instruments preceding it. That general-versus-specific reach is arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Laws' is used lightly (Sections 2.2, 2.6, 6.6, 9.3) and nothing contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Precise statutory citation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The recital's mangled reference to the same statute is the only wrinkle, and this definition cures it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear on its face: written approval or affirmative vote of a majority of Member Votes.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Agreement also defines the near-identical 'Majority' (c021) and uses the two interchangeably in Section 5.5(vii)-(xi), creating avoidable slippage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Majority' is defined as a quantum of votes yet used in Section 5.5(vii) as if it were persons ('A Majority present in person or by proxy'). That mismatch is visible in use.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its coexistence with 'Majority Vote' in Sections 5.1 and 5.5 leaves it uncertain which standard governs a given action.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definition folds Directors into 'Manager', which is intelligible though slightly circular.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.1 confirms Directors are designated Managers, so the pieces fit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defining 'Members' as 'two (2) or more of such Persons' is odd and would leave plural provisions inoperative if only one member remained.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.2(ii) contemplates a member ceasing to be a member with remaining Members continuing, which sits awkwardly with a two-member floor.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Simple pointer to Schedule A.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Schedule A does allocate 49/51 votes, but Section 16.6 speaks of 'LLC Votes', an undefined variant of this term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any amounts determined by the Members to be necessary to provide a reasonable reserve for working-capital needs or any other contingencies' is an open-ended discretionary carve-out that can swallow distributions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reserves are set by the Members here while Section 9.2 vests distribution decisions in the Board, and Section 10.2 mandates accrual accounting while this definition mandates cash-basis determination.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One-line circular definition, unremarkable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article VII supplies the offices.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition fixes Percentage Interest by Schedule A yet also 'as determined by the unanimous written consent of the Members as adjusted from time to time', two different sources of truth in one sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.1(iii) lets the Secretary unilaterally update Schedule A and says such revision is not an amendment, which cuts against the unanimous-consent requirement here and against Section 17.10.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list reads 'any individual, Company, association...' where 'corporation' was plainly intended, and 'Company' is a defined term meaning Dialogo, LLC — a mechanical error that distorts the definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read literally it would make every 'Person' reference circular against the 'Company' definition, though context repairs it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Ties Profits and Losses to taxable income under §703(a); definite though thin (no book/tax adjustments).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 10.2's accrual mandate and Section 8.2's methods are consistent enough.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear cross-reference to Section 7.4 duties.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.1 has Officers elected by the Board and Section 2.6 gives the Secretary filing authority, all consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure cross-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 11.1 supplies the designation (DMSA).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard regulatory definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently in Article VIII.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate headings clause, definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Given the duplicated 'Section 6.6' headings and stray cross-references, this clause helps rather than conflicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Mostly mechanical formation language; the statement that Schedule A revisions 'shall not be deemed an amendment to this Agreement' is a striking carve-out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That carve-out is in tension with Section 17.10 (all amendments require unanimous written execution) and with the Percentage Interest definition's unanimous-consent requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Name and alternate-name authority are stated plainly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.6 assigns related fictitious-name filings to the Board and Secretary, consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Continue in perpetuity, unless the Company is dissolved' is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article XV's dissolution events are expressly preserved by the 'unless' clause, so no incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Straightforward designation of registered agent and office.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It gives the change power to 'the Members' while Sections 2.5 and 2.6 give comparable powers to the Board, a small allocation inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A specific address and a clear power to relocate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 17.1(i) and Section 10.1 key off this address, consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any jurisdiction in which the Company transacts business' versus 'may wish to conduct business' is loose but workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.2 and 3.2(i)(a).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A narrow stated object ('developing Spanish language newspaper(s) and media') is immediately followed by an all-purpose catch-all ('any lawful act or activity'), leaving the scope of 'the business' genuinely uncertain. That general-versus-specific tension is exactly the sort courts construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12.7 bars LSB from services 'to the extent it relates to the business' and permits DMSA to compete, so the reach of this purpose clause directly drives that restriction's meaning.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long enumerated powers list opened by 'including, but not limited to', with several transcription slips; the enumeration is conventional corporate boilerplate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Many enumerated powers (borrowing, disposing of assets, contracts with Members) are subjected to unanimous Board approval by Section 6.8, so the grant must be read subject to that limit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite: merger requires approval of all Members.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.8 lists many actions requiring unanimous Board approval but omits merger, and Section 5.1 vests residual power in Members, so this fits without conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It defers entirely to Schedule A for amounts, and Schedule A's LSB entry ('$00,001.00') is on its face garbled.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.8(iii) contemplates reimbursing DMSA for 'initial capital contributions', which sits oddly with the fixed contributions and Percentage Interests recorded here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two definite propositions of law, standard in LLC agreements.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 5.3's partition waiver.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Subsection (ii)(a) is mangled — 'the respective invoices of each of DMSA', 'payment form such customer' — and (b) uses 'Membership Interests', a term the Agreement never defines. The invoice carve-out's scope (services 'through or on behalf of the Company for a client') is also indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The profit-payment promise in (ii)(b) collides with Section 9.2 (Board decides distributions) and Section 6.8(iii) (unanimous Board approval for distributions other than DMSA reimbursement), and 'Membership Interests' does not match the defined 'Percentage Interest'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and mechanical, though the Regulation citation is truncated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches the Capital Account definition and Section 15.3's liquidation by Capital Account balances.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Subject to such terms and conditions acceptable to the Company and each Member' leaves the advance's terms to be agreed, but the operative consequences are stated clearly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 4.3(iii) and 15.3(i) (Members who are creditors paid first).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Members have the power to exercise any and all other rights or powers of the Company' is a sweeping residual grant whose boundary against Board authority is unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.1 vests management in the Board but is expressly 'Subject to Section 5.1', producing a circular allocation of authority between Members and Board.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All ordinary and necessary out-of-pocket expenses incurred by the Members on behalf of the Company' is a standard but boundary-less category, with no approval mechanism.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.3(ii) bars any payment to Members except three listed exceptions, which do not include expense reimbursement, and Section 6.8(xiv) requires unanimous approval for incurring obligations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence waiver, definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 4.2 (no interest in specific Company property).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Flat prohibition, clear on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.2(ii) expressly treats the 'resignation' of a Member as a dissolution event, which presupposes a resignation this section forbids — a genuine internal inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long procedural section; subsection (i) says special meetings 'may be held at such time and place, and shall be stated in the notice', a garbled sentence, and no annual meeting date is fixed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subsection (xi) permits action by written consent signed by 'a Majority' even though other provisions (Sections 4.1(ii), 13.1, 17.10, 3.2(ii)) demand unanimity, though the 'unless otherwise provided' opener largely reconciles them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A Manager by the Members for purposes of the Act' uses 'the Act', a label the Agreement never defines (the defined term is 'Maine Act'). The rest is standard board-composition language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Making Board management 'Subject to Section 5.1', which itself gives Members residual power over all Company rights, leaves the management allocation circular; election of Directors also tracks Section 5.5(ii).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed notice mechanics; 'by any other means of communication' is a loose catch-all after a specific list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 6.3, 6.4 and 17.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It carves out 'Section 6.9 of this Agreement', a section that does not exist in the instrument, and provides a tie-break procedure for a three-Director board where a tie is structurally unlikely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The intended cross-reference is evidently Section 6.8 (unanimous Board actions), and the tie-break sending matters to the Members cuts against Section 6.8's unanimity requirement and Section 6.1's Board management.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear telephonic-participation rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors Section 5.5(x) for Members; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Committees may exercise 'all the powers and authority of the Board', limited only by a reference to 'Section 6.9', which does not exist. That dangling limitation is a mechanical defect with substantive effect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The intended restraint is Section 6.8's unanimous-approval list; as drafted a one-Director committee could take actions Section 6.8 reserves to a unanimous Board.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Ordinary compensation language, but it is numbered 'Section 6.6' and so is the next section, a numbering error.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Board-fixed Director compensation sits against Section 6.8(x), which requires unanimous Board approval for contracts with Directors, and against Section 4.3(ii)'s no-salary rule for Members.
